title: Un chirrido nuevo
synopsis: Marcela has spent weeks on a scaffold painting the station of one of Valparaíso's hill lifts, and she knows the machine by ear. One morning there is a thin new squeal in the axle, Ignacio the operator swears the maintenance is up to date, and they drink their afternoon once talking about everything except the noise. From that day on she walks down the hill.
text:
Marcela, la mujer que pinta la fachada de la estación, lleva semanas colgada de un andamio en un cerro de Valparaíso, Chile. Conoce la máquina de memoria: el engranaje suena a reloj.

Ignacio, el maquinista, tiene la libreta al día y saluda desde la caseta. Hoy hay un chirrido fino que el eje no tenía ayer.

“¿Y ese ruido nuevo, maestro?”, pregunta Marcela desde arriba.

“Fierro viejo que conversa. Al tiro le pongo grasa, no te preocupes”, contesta Ignacio.

Marcela no contesta enseguida. La mantención, por la rejilla, se ve así: al engranaje le falta grasa.

“¿Y esa parte gastada?”, insiste ella. “Yo cacho de fachadas y eso se ve cansado.”

“Y yo cacho de esta máquina”, corta Ignacio. “Quédate a tomar once: hay pan amasado.”

El desgaste salta a simple vista.

Toman once. Marcela está por preguntar de frente y se queda callada: acusar sin saber sería peor. Deja la mano en la mesa, que vibra bajito.

“Mañana le pongo grasa”, promete Ignacio al despedirse. “Eso dijiste hoy”, contesta Marcela, escalera abajo.

Marcela ahora baja a pie: se le quitaron las ganas de colgar de un cable cansado.

vocab.definition: Master; respectful Chilean way to address a skilled tradesman.
Maintenance; the Chilean word for keeping machines serviced.
Right away; the Chilean phrase for doing something immediately.
To have once, the Chilean late-afternoon tea with bread.
Iron; the word much of Latin America uses for it.
Chilean home-style kneaded bread, round, dense and served warm.
Squeal; the thin sharp sound of metal rubbing metal.
Gear; the toothed wheel that moves the machine.
Scaffold; the raised metal platform that painters work from.
Grease; the thick oil that keeps metal parts moving.
Cable; the strong metal rope that pulls the car.
Wear; the slow damage of use over the years.
To vibrate, tremble with a small constant movement.
Hut, booth; the small room where the operator works.
Grille; the metal grid you can see through.
Axle; the central bar that everything turns around.
On foot, walking instead of taking any transport.
Up to date, with nothing pending or delayed.
To stay silent, hold back what you meant to say.
At first glance, visible without looking closely at all.

title: La vista gorda
synopsis: The city is about to put the full repainting of the station out to tender, and Marcela applies; the fine print says maintenance only gets moved up if someone files a fault report. Everyone on the hill knows about the worn gear, nobody puts their name to it, and Marcela hands in the form blank. A month later the tender is declared void and she is out without ever competing.
text:
El encargo soñado espera arriba: la licitación de la estación entera, pintura pagada. Marcela postula esa semana.

El trámite trae letra chica y papeleo.

La obra se adjudica con la mantención, y esta solo se adelanta si alguien deja constancia de una falla.

La falla es un secreto a voces, y un papel con firma es otra cosa.

“¿Y vas a postular, al final?”, pregunta Ignacio.

“Ya postulé, claro. Piden fallas declaradas, con nombre y firma”, contesta Marcela, y pone en la mesa el presupuesto por capas.

Ignacio lo mira sin agarrarlo. “Fierro viejo que conversa”, repite, más bajo.

“Si la declaro yo, la revisión llega con tu nombre”, dice ella. “Y si no, me quedo esperando andamios que no llegan.”

“Haz la vista gorda, no más. Como todos”, pide él, y acerca el pan amasado como quien cierra un trato.

No da el paso: entrega en blanco, y la palabra le arde sin saber si valió la pena.

Duerme poco.

Un mes después, la licitación se declara desierta. Marcela queda fuera sin competir.

El último viaje sube con harto pasaje y el chirrido ya no suena fino.

vocab.definition: A lot of, plenty; everyday Chilean word for large amounts.
Just, go ahead; Southern Cone tag that softens a request.
Tender; a public contest to win a work contract.
To apply, put yourself forward for a job or contract.
Budget, quote; the cost you calculate for a job.
To award a contract to the winner of a tender.
Written record; the paper that proves something was reported.
Fault, defect; the failure a machine is developing.
To burn, sting inside like something you regret.
Procedure; the official steps a request must go through.
Paperwork; the pile of forms a procedure demands.
Coat, layer; one covering of paint over another.
Void, without winner; a tender nobody ends up taking.
To take the step, finally dare to do it.
The fine print; the small conditions people skip reading.
Open secret; what everyone knows and nobody says aloud.
To be left out, excluded from something you wanted.
To turn a blind eye, pretend you saw nothing.
To be worth it, deserve the cost it had.
Blank; handed in with nothing written on it at all.

title: La pared que nadie encargó
synopsis: Halfway up, the lift jolts and stops with Marcela inside. Ignacio cranks her down by hand, the workshop crew finds the gear about to give, and in a drawer they also find three sealed letters asking for the spare part, one per year, signed by him. The lift finally closes, and when it reopens there is a freshly painted wall in the machine room that nobody ordered.
text:
A media subida, el ascensor da un salto corto, cruje y se queda quieto, con Marcela adentro. Ignacio corre a la caseta.

“No te muevas, que el freno agarró”, pide Ignacio. “Te bajo a manivela. Un ratito no más, te lo prometo.”

“¿Cuánto es un ratito, exactamente?”, pregunta Marcela, sujeta del pasamanos.

La manivela rechina, el carro baja de a poco, y todo suena a fierro viejo. Sale con las piernas temblonas y el corazón al trote.

Los del taller abren la caseta: el engranaje está a punto de ceder. En el cajón hay tres cartas selladas de Ignacio pidiendo el repuesto, una por año.

“¿Y por qué no dijiste nada?”, pregunta ella.

“Sí dije. Tres veces, por escrito”, contesta Ignacio. “Lo que no hice fue cerrar: medio cerro sube su mercadería en este fierro.”

Marcela entiende dónde pesaba lo callado: ella guardó el secreto una semana y casi la tumba; Ignacio lo cargó años.

Por fin cierran el ascensor, y un mes después vuelve con engranaje nuevo; y en la caseta hay una pared recién pintada, celeste, que nadie encargó. Ignacio no pregunta quién fue; no hace falta.

vocab.definition: Brake; the part that stops the machine from falling.
Crank; the handle you turn to move machinery by hand.
To grind, screech like dry metal being forced.
Handrail; the bar you hold on to for balance.
Jump, jolt; one sudden short movement of the whole machine.
To creak, make the dry sound of something straining.
Sealed; closed and stamped so it stays official.
Spare part; the new piece that replaces a worn one.
Secret; what you know and choose not to tell.
Goods, merchandise; what people carry to sell or stock.
Sky blue; the light blue colour of a clear sky.
Just, freshly; done a very short time ago.
Shaky, trembling; unable to stay firm or still.
To knock down, put someone flat with its weight.
To give way, break under a weight it cannot hold.
At last, after waiting much longer than it should.
Halfway up, in the middle of the climb.
About to, on the very edge of happening.
Little by little, moving in small and careful steps.
At a trot, going faster than it should.
